tolerance_html:
mechloop/tolerance/process.py holds, per process, the standard deviations the tolerance verifier built its 3000 simulated machines with. The sheets hold the fabricator to +/-2 standard deviations of the same figures, so a batch of parts inside the drawing tolerance is the population that was simulated. A part AT the limit everywhere is worse than what was simulated: the limits are not a licence to sit on them.

printing_html:
• Printer assumed by the manufacture verifier: build volume (220.0, 220.0, 220.0), nozzle 0.4 mm, layer 0.2 (the verifier default: the design does not declare one) mm.
  • Orientation: pinned per part in the design (print_up), listed below; the STL is already turned so the bed face is on Z = 0.
  • Walls and infill: not declared by the design. The verifier's mass and time estimate used: None.
  • The FEA load cases treat every printed part as solid, isotropic material. A part printed at 20 % infill is not the part that was analysed. For the parts with a load case (), print solid or accept that the factor of safety is unverified.
  • No threads in plastic, no heat-set inserts: every screw in a printed part runs into a steel nut (captive pockets and slots are in the models).
  • Printed clearance holes are drawn at ISO 273 medium + 0.2 mm FDM allowance (M2.5 3.1, M3 3.6, M4 4.7, M5 5.7, M6 6.8; +0.3 and a teardrop or flat top for a hole whose axis lies in the build plane): vertical holes print undersize. Starting values: print a coupon of M3 holes 3.4 to 3.8 in 0.1 mm steps on the printer that will make the parts, then set the allowance and the slicer's hole compensation (docs/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md). Bearing seats and insert pockets are drawn to their own figures.

parts.name: carriage_plate_left
parts.desc: Carriage plate (left): one of three identical flat 1.6 mm 6061 plates. Its top 20 mm is bolted to the 2020 square's outer face (two M5, T-nuts); its bottom carries the guide block z_carriage_left (four M3 x 5 into the block's own threads). The 30 mm web between them is a flexure: stiff along the wall, soft square to it (251 N/mm), so this block locates the carrier along the wall only and a rail that is not exactly parallel, or a carrier that has grown warm, bends the web instead of loading the block.

parts.name: carriage_plate_rear
parts.desc: Carriage plate (rear): one of three identical flat 1.6 mm 6061 plates. Its top 20 mm is bolted to the 2020 square's outer face (two M5, T-nuts); its bottom carries the guide block z_carriage_rear (four M3 x 5 into the block's own threads). The 30 mm web between them is a flexure: stiff along the wall, soft square to it (251 N/mm), so this block locates the carrier along the wall only and a rail that is not exactly parallel, or a carrier that has grown warm, bends the web instead of loading the block.

parts.name: nut_plate
parts.desc: Laser-cut 6061 nut plate under the carrier's square. How the bed is lifted: the POM anti-backlash nut z_nut (supplied on the motor's screw; dimensions a STAND-IN) rides lead screw leadscrew. Its square flange is under this 9.525 mm plate, which is bolted under the 2020 square's member sq_rear (two M5 from below into T-nuts) and reaches 56.2 mm out to the screw; the nut's barrel hangs below. The carrier's weight rests on the flange, so when the screw turns the nut climbs it and lifts the plate, the square, the deck and the bed. The M2.5 pin screw nut_pin (through a 5 mm aluminium sleeve, fixed in a corner hole of the flange) sits in a radial slot in the plate: it stops the nut turning with the screw while letting it float 2 mm sideways. The nut is captive: the laser-cut keeper nut_keeper, bolted 0.1 mm under the flange on two M3 through-bolts and spacers, stops the plate lifting off it.

parts.name: nut_plate_fl
parts.desc: Laser-cut 6061 nut plate under the carrier's square. How the bed is lifted: the POM anti-backlash nut z_nut_fl (supplied on the motor's screw; dimensions a STAND-IN) rides lead screw leadscrew_fl. Its square flange is under this 9.525 mm plate, which is bolted under the 2020 square's member sq_left (two M5 from below into T-nuts) and reaches 9.1 mm out to the screw; the nut's barrel hangs below. The carrier's weight rests on the flange, so when the screw turns the nut climbs it and lifts the plate, the square, the deck and the bed. The M2.5 pin screw nut_pin_fl (through a 5 mm aluminium sleeve, fixed in a corner hole of the flange) sits in a radial slot in the plate: it stops the nut turning with the screw while letting it float 2 mm sideways. The nut is captive: the laser-cut keeper nut_keeper_fl, bolted 0.1 mm under the flange on two M3 through-bolts and spacers, stops the plate lifting off it.

parts.name: z_nut_fr
parts.desc: POM anti-backlash nut, floating and captive under nut_plate_fr. How the bed is lifted: the POM anti-backlash nut z_nut_fr (supplied on the motor's screw; dimensions a STAND-IN) rides lead screw leadscrew_fr. Its square flange is under this 9.525 mm plate, which is bolted under the 2020 square's member sq_right (two M5 from below into T-nuts) and reaches 9.1 mm out to the screw; the nut's barrel hangs below. The carrier's weight rests on the flange, so when the screw turns the nut climbs it and lifts the plate, the square, the deck and the bed. The M2.5 pin screw nut_pin_fr (through a 5 mm aluminium sleeve, fixed in a corner hole of the flange) sits in a radial slot in the plate: it stops the nut turning with the screw while letting it float 2 mm sideways. The nut is captive: the laser-cut keeper nut_keeper_fr, bolted 0.1 mm under the flange on two M3 through-bolts and spacers, stops the plate lifting off it.

findings.message: Bed probe 'bed_probe': a unit at the short end of its spread (switching distance 4 mm on steel (BTT Eddy manual (vendor_docs/BTT_Eddy_Series_User_Manual_20250507.pdf) 4.1: mounted 2-3 mm above the tip, coil current calibrated at 20 mm, so it reads over at least 2-20 mm; Klipper probe_eddy_current triggers at the height PROBE_EDDY_CURRENT_CALIBRATE sets: 4 mm is a setting inside that range), +/-10% unit to unit (from its ratings)) switches with the nozzle 1.10 mm above the bed as drawn. The toolhead's stack-up between face and tip (0.95 mm, 99.7 %) and the bed's flatness over the 37.02 mm between them (0.23 mm) add up to 1.19 mm: with the face that much too high, or the bed that much higher under the nozzle, the nozzle touches first.
findings.hint: Lower the face (it may come down to 1.19 mm above the tip), use a sensor with more range on this bed, or set the sensor's height on the built machine with its nuts against a gauge and say so in the build instructions (that removes the stack-up, not the bed's flatness).

findings.message: Bed probe 'bed_probe' is offset (-8, 36.146) mm from the nozzle and kept 15.3 mm inside the plate edge, so strips of the print area are never probed: {'x_high': 8.0, 'y_low': np.float64(36.15), 'y_high': np.float64(9.35)} (mm wide; print area declared: design.printer['print_area'] = 186.6 x 208.1 mm, centred on the plate). The firmware holds the nearest measured value there.
findings.hint: Acceptable if the bed is flat at the edges; otherwise move the probe closer to the nozzle or shrink the print area.

open_items.rank_label: would stop the build (or is a safety matter)
open_items.title: Bed probe on a thin spring-steel sheet: sensing distance unverified
open_items.known: Every probe figure (z_offset 1.5 mm, range [1.1, 1.9], face window [1.186, 2.414] mm) assumes the sensor switches at 4.0 mm, the maker's figure for a 1 mm iron target. The target here is 220 x 220 mm textured PEI spring-steel print sheet, held on bed_magnet by magnetism alone: lift it off to remove prints. (a catalogue part) on its magnetic base. Basis recorded by the report: BTT Eddy manual (vendor_docs/BTT_Eddy_Series_User_Manual_20250507.pdf) 4.1: mounted 2-3 mm above the tip, coil current calibrated at 20 mm, so it reads over at least 2-20 mm; Klipper probe_eddy_current triggers at the height PROBE_EDDY_CURRENT_CALIBRATE sets: 4 mm is a setting inside that range.
open_items.check: COMMISSIONING.md step B1 with the real sensor, sheet and magnet BEFORE ordering anything else; pass window there

open_items.rank_label: would stop the build (or is a safety matter)
open_items.title: Mains side: printed hoods only, one bonded extrusion, not certified
open_items.known: Open frame; the inlet's rear, the relay module and the supply terminals are under printed hoods (mains_cover_psu, mains_cover_psu_screw_0, mains_cover_psu_screw_0_washer, mains_cover_psu_screw_0_nwasher, mains_cover_psu_screw_0_nut, mains_cover_psu_screw_1, mains_cover_psu_screw_1_washer, mains_cover_psu_screw_1_nwasher, mains_cover_psu_screw_1_nut, mains_cover_inlet, mains_cover_inlet_screw_0, mains_cover_inlet_screw_0_washer, mains_cover_inlet_screw_0_nwasher, mains_cover_inlet_screw_0_nut, mains_cover_inlet_screw_1, mains_cover_inlet_screw_1_washer, mains_cover_inlet_screw_1_nwasher, mains_cover_inlet_screw_1_nut) that are open where the wires enter: touch protection depends on fully insulated receptacles and the hoods being fitted. The model earths the supply and one extrusion; everything else relies on anodised joints. The supply has a 115 / 230 V selector that must be set by hand.
open_items.check: WIRING.md mains section; continuity test E1; a competent person signs off the mains side

open_items.rank_label: would stop the build (or is a safety matter)
open_items.title: Build 1 is staged: order and build stage 1 first
open_items.known: Every part carries its build stage (1 frame, electronics bay, bed and Z; 2 gantry, toolhead and probe; 3 feedback hardware). The DG-07 placeholders left in stage 1 are listed at the top of this package; stage 2 and 3 placeholders are allowed now and listed with them.
open_items.check: run python -m mechloop.sourcing --design designs/printer_v12.py and order stage 1's long-lead lines first

open_items.rank_label: would stop the build (or is a safety matter)
open_items.title: Commissioning: probe only after the bed has soaked at temperature
open_items.known: Limit (b) is worked on the warming that is left after the soak (the START_PRINT macro holds it: M190, then the soak, then G28, Z_TILT_ADJUST, BED_MESH_CALIBRATE). The carrier's time constant is an estimate.
open_items.check: measure the nozzle-gap drift with the probe over 30 min after the bed reaches temperature; set the soak to what the drift needs

open_items.rank_label: would stop the build (or is a safety matter)
open_items.title: MIC-6 flatness is a receiving check (owner: accept 0.13 mm, reject worse)
open_items.known: Limit (a) uses 0.127 mm for the plate as bought; the maker's brochure gives 0.381 mm for this thickness.
open_items.check: straight edge and feelers on the cut plate on arrival; reject a worse piece

open_items.rank_label: would stop the build (or is a safety matter)
open_items.title: Mains: contactor switched from the Pi; earth star at the frame stud
open_items.known: Finder 22.32 (L and N) with a 120 V coil through the Phoenix PLC-RSC-5DC/21, whose coil a Pi GPIO drives through a PN2222A (1 kOhm); Moonraker [power printer] with off_when_shutdown. 16 AWG earth: inlet PE -> frame stud; supply FG and bed plate each on their own lug.
open_items.check: continuity test of every earth bond to the inlet's PE pin before first mains power; check the contactor drops on a Klipper shutdown

open_items.rank_label: would stop the build (or is a safety matter)
open_items.title: Wham Bam 220 PEI plate was sold out on 2026-11-20
open_items.known: The magnetic base is in stock at the maker.
open_items.check: order when restocked, or choose another 220 x 220 0.4 mm spring-steel PEI plate with a published thickness

open_items.rank_label: would stop the build (or is a safety matter)
open_items.title: Z screws at full length stand close to the frame
open_items.known: Used as sold (330 mm), the screws' tops are at 400 to 401 mm. The front two stand 1.5 mm inboard of the top side rails' inner faces and 2.5 mm outboard of the X beam's ends, free at the top; the rear one stands outside the back wall. Run-out or whip of more than about 1 mm at the top would let a front screw touch the top side rail.
open_items.check: check each screw's run-out at its tip on arrival (motor running slowly); run the bed through its whole travel by hand before first power

open_items.rank_label: would stop the build (or is a safety matter)
open_items.title: Screw lengths in T-slots rest on Misumi's drawings, without tolerances
open_items.known: Slot 6.0 deep, 2.0 lip (Misumi HFS5, confirmed by Misumi's STEP), T-nut HNTAJ5. 24 screws now have between 0.5 d and 0.8 d of thread (the owner chose M5 x 8 with one washer); on a shallower slot of another make 94 screws would end closer than 0.5 mm to the floor.
open_items.check: buy Misumi HFS5-2020 and HNTAJ5 nuts, or measure what is bought and re-run verify

open_items.rank_label: would stop the build (or is a safety matter)
open_items.title: Probe supply lead is not a wire in the electrical model
open_items.known: the sensor's +24 V lead is declared on the device only: no length, no BOM metres, no loom check; the diode's place is not defined
open_items.check: add about the 'bed probe' wire's length of one more conductor to the order and decide where the diode sits

open_items.rank_label: would stop the build (or is a safety matter)
open_items.title: The simulated assembly order cannot be followed by a person; the guide's stage order is unchecked
open_items.known: mechloop assemble finds an order valid for access in which 0 units are placed before anything supports them (frame posts and corner brackets come last, the machine is turned over 26 times). ASSEMBLY.md re-groups the units frame-first; that order was not run through the access checker. Also absent from the simulation and its 171.1 min: belts, wiring, bonding (T-nuts and bracket screws are in it).
open_items.check: dry-fit each stage; where a screw cannot be reached in stage order, note it and fit that part earlier

open_items.rank_label: would stop the build (or is a safety matter)
open_items.title: Report warning, electrical `cutoff_depends_on_mcu`
open_items.known: Heater 'extruder': a shorted MOSFET is survived only because the firmware drops the supply relay (peak 282 degC). There is no cut-off that works if the controller has also hung.
open_items.check: see docs/PRINTER_V12.md for the designer's reading

open_items.title: x_belt: in plane in 95.9% of builds against a requirement of 98%
open_items.known: Margin -2.1% with a sampling error of 0.36%: not distinguishable from the limit. 99 % of builds within 1.46 mm.
open_items.check: sight along each Y belt after tensioning: it must run in the middle of both pulleys' flanges over the whole travel; shim the idler if not

open_items.title: Lead-screw nut float: 2.16 mm needed, 1.8 mm provided
open_items.known: 99th percentile of the simulated builds, worst screw: leadscrew 2.16 mm, leadscrew_fl 2.03 mm, leadscrew_fr 1.53 mm. A nut that runs out of float side-loads its screw (1174.0 N in the un-floated case).
open_items.check: ASSEMBLY.md, float check at bottom, middle and top of travel

open_items.title: Z rails are parallel in 24% of builds as built: the machine depends on the alignment step
open_items.known: Out of parallel by up to 0.952 mm (99 %) against the maker's 0.009 mm; the tolerance verifier accepts this because a rail_align adjustment is declared. The extrusions' straightness is not catalogued and not included; the rails' accuracy class is assumed.
open_items.check: ASSEMBLY.md rail_align; commissioning M3

open_items.title: Y rails are parallel in 0% of builds as built: the machine depends on the alignment step
open_items.known: Out of parallel by up to 1.205 mm (99 %) against the maker's 0.009 mm; the tolerance verifier accepts this because a rail_align adjustment is declared. The extrusions' straightness is not catalogued and not included; the rails' accuracy class is assumed.
open_items.check: ASSEMBLY.md rail_align; commissioning M3

open_items.title: Bed level may change by up to None mm over the Z travel (formula; disputed)
open_items.known: Rail class None; block spacing None mm. The designer's note says the formula ignores the three screws, which hold the tilt. Unresolved by simulation.
open_items.check: commissioning M7 settles it

open_items.title: Report warning, interference `tnut_thread_engagement_marginal`
open_items.known: 32 screw(s) have between 0.5 d and 0.8 d of thread in their T-nut (least: z_deck_bolt_0, 2.52 mm = 0.50 d) and do not pass the nut's whole thread: the nut is not used to its maker's rating. Tighten to a reduced torque or use the next screw length.
open_items.check: A longer standard screw that still ends clear of the slot floor, or one washer fewer; otherwise state a reduced torque.

open_items.title: Report warning, interference `tslot_profile_sensitive`
open_items.known: 30 screw(s) pass on the slot and T-nut geometry used but not on '2020 slot 6, B-type (community STEP) + Misumi HNTAJ5 nut' (slot 5.3 mm deep, lip 1.5 mm): 30 would end within 0.5 mm of that floor or on it, 0 would have under 0.5 d of thread; worst: y_tension_anchor_screw_a (-0.20 mm from the floor, 0.64 d). Measure what is bought before fitting these.
open_items.check: Put the bought extrusion's and T-nut's figures in mechloop/parts/vendor/tslot_2020_hardware.json and run verify again.

open_items.title: Report warning, tolerance `sheet_bends_not_recognised`

open_items.title: Report warning, subsystems `probe_trigger_margin_thin`
open_items.known: Bed probe 'bed_probe': a unit at the short end of its spread (switching distance 4 mm on steel (BTT Eddy manual (vendor_docs/BTT_Eddy_Series_User_Manual_20250507.pdf) 4.1: mounted 2-3 mm above the tip, coil current calibrated at 20 mm, so it reads over at least 2-20 mm; Klipper probe_eddy_current triggers at the height PROBE_EDDY_CURRENT_CALIBRATE sets: 4 mm is a setting inside that range), +/-10% unit to unit (from its ratings)) switches with the nozzle 1.10 mm above the bed as drawn.
